title: Great books and their authors
description: Authors, dates, literary movements and famous lines, from Molière to Stephen King.

content.title: A walk through the library
content.body: From Molière's comedies in the 17th century to today's novels, these questions travel through French and English-language literature. Some are easy, some are traps: read every choice before answering!

content.question: Jules Verne, the author of Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas, lived...
content.explanation: Jules Verne (1828-1905) wrote his "Extraordinary Voyages", such as Journey to the Centre of the Earth and Around the World in Eighty Days. 1802-1870 are the dates of Alexandre Dumas.

content.question:
Stephen King's The Gunslinger (1982) opens with this sentence:

"The man in black fled across the desert, and the ___ followed."
content.explanation: The gunslinger is Roland Deschain, and The Gunslinger is the first volume of the Dark Tower saga.

content.question: In which year was the first Harry Potter book published?
content.explanation: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone by J.K. Rowling came out in 1997. 2001 is the year of the first film.

content.question: Honoré de Balzac gathered almost all his novels, such as Father Goriot, into one huge work. Which one?
content.explanation: Balzac (1799-1850) wanted to paint the whole French society of his time: that is realism. The Rougon-Macquart is Zola's cycle, In Search of Lost Time is Proust's, and Les Misérables is Hugo's.

content.question: In 1898, Émile Zola published a famous open letter defending Captain Dreyfus. What was its title?
content.explanation: "J'accuse...!" appeared in the newspaper L'Aurore. Germinal is one of Zola's novels, Le Cid is a play by Corneille and Candide a tale by Voltaire.

content.question: In his essay Comme un roman (The Rights of the Reader), Daniel Pennac lists ten rights of the reader. Which of these are among them?

choices.text: The duty to finish every book you start
The right to read only the books a teacher approved

content.explanation: The ten rights also include the right not to finish a book, the right to read it again and the right to read out loud. Pennac is also the author of the Malaussène novels, such as The Fairy Gunmother.

content.question:
Complete this line by Oscar Wilde:

"I can resist everything except ___."
content.explanation: It comes from his play Lady Windermere's Fan (1892). Wilde (1854-1900) was known for his wit.

content.question: In Oscar Wilde's The Picture of Dorian Gray, what grows old and ugly instead of Dorian?
content.explanation: Dorian stays young and beautiful while his painted portrait shows his age and his sins. The novel is a landmark of aestheticism, the movement of "art for art's sake".

content.question: In Edgar Allan Poe's most famous poem, which bird keeps repeating "Nevermore"?
content.explanation: The Raven was published in 1845. Poe (1809-1849) also invented the detective story, and his tales were translated into French by Baudelaire.

content.question: George Orwell (1903-1950), author of Nineteen Eighty-Four, was a pen name. What was his real name?
content.explanation: Eric Blair wrote Animal Farm (1945) and Nineteen Eighty-Four (1949), with its famous "Big Brother is watching you". Huxley wrote another dystopia, Brave New World.

content.question: In The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy by Douglas Adams, what is the Answer to the Ultimate Question of Life, the Universe, and Everything?
content.explanation: A supercomputer thinks for seven and a half million years to find 42. "Don't Panic" is the advice written on the cover of the Guide.

content.question: "All for one, one for all!" is the motto of the heroes of...

choices.text: The Three Musketeers, by Alexandre Dumas
The Count of Monte Cristo, by Alexandre Dumas
Treasure Island, by Robert Louis Stevenson

content.explanation: Dumas (1802-1870) published The Three Musketeers in 1844, the same year he started The Count of Monte Cristo.

content.question: In Mary Shelley's novel (1818), who is Frankenstein?

choices.text: Victor Frankenstein, the scientist who creates the creature
The creature made from dead bodies
The village where the story happens

content.explanation: The creature has no name. The subtitle of this Gothic novel, often called the first science fiction novel, is "The Modern Prometheus".

content.question: Which prize did Michel Houellebecq win in 2010 for The Map and the Territory?
content.explanation: The Goncourt is the most famous French literary prize. Houellebecq is also known for Atomised (Les Particules élémentaires) and Submission.

content.question: Molière (1622-1673), author of Tartuffe and The Miser, was a stage name. What was his real name?
content.explanation: French is sometimes called "the language of Molière". François-Marie Arouet is Voltaire's real name; Racine and Corneille wrote tragedies in the same century.

content.question: Who wrote The Red and the Black (1830), the story of the ambitious Julien Sorel?
content.explanation: Stendhal was the pen name of Henri Beyle (1783-1842). He also wrote The Charterhouse of Parma.

content.instructions: Match each book with its author.
